items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: playing with a group called Hal Smith’s Roadrunners... Hal Smith, myself and Keith had made some trio albums together.

ctx.x: I think most musicians end up doing some of that, they may not talk about it an awful lot. When was the first — do you have a gig or a series of gigs with a certain person that you felt was really your entrance into let’s say the big time or really doing what you wanted to?

Well what I’m doing now is what I really enjoy. I’ve never enjoyed anything so much because I’m getting a chance to play with musicians that are great New York musicians, and as I say again, a lot of them are here today: Scott Robinson, Marty Grosz, Keith Ingham, Hal Smith. Just in the last ten or fifteen years I’ve been getting into that type of music and being lucky enough to make a lot of recordings with Marty and do a lot of appearances. I’ve been to Japan twice. I’d say this is the most musical feeling I’ve…

Muggsy Spanier and I played with Eddie Condon and Bobby Hackett and Jimmy McPartland. That was just little stints, eight weeks here, maybe sixteen weeks there, three weeks there. But now that I’m doing a lot of recordings with Marty and we have a little group called The Orphan Newsboys, I’m really at my happiest experiences right now.

items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: So when I, for instance with the Road Runners, Bobby Gordon’s got his regular job in San Diego... But he also works with Marty Grosz... So I’ve got to coordinate that.

ctx.x: You’ve done quite a bit of band leading. What’s the biggest headache in being a band leader? The biggest thing to surmount?

Coordinating everyone’s schedules. Because nobody can give their loyalty to one band. So when I, for instance with the Road Runners, Bobby Gordon’s got his regular job in San Diego and now it’s only two nights a week. But he also works with Marty Grosz and the Orphan Newsboys, and plays jazz parties as a solo. So I’ve got to coordinate that. Rebecca works all the time in Portland, freelance and with Dave Frishberg, and she’s on this jazz party circuit. So that’s enough right there. Then the other two guys are…
And now you’re going to be even more spread out, because you’re going to be in New Orleans.
